item.title: Staff Post - Wikiwalk Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

When I was reading this initially, I was reminded of SCP-2082s ability to cause such storms as those described in this article. The SCP Foundation is likely to look into a potential connection between these phenomena. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

SCP-880 exhibits several abnormal characteristics, most notably what appears to be a nearly constant blizzard, breaking for an average of 1-2 hours daily. Analysis of this event has determined SCP-880 experiences no snowfall, and intense winds have produced various squalls which cause the illusion of a blizzard. Despite the potential of snow drifts within SCP-880, no level of snow deeper than sixteen (16) centimetres has been found within SCP-880 or in the surrounding area. Anything entering SCP-880 during a storm or within when a storm begins has so far proven to be irrevocably lost, despite extensive search and rescue efforts. GPS location fails shortly after a storm begins, transmission and rescue lines are cut, and radio communication becomes impossible due to overwhelming interference. Current tallies set the number of personnel lost to SCP-880 at 32.

To this:

SCP-880 exhibits several abnormal characteristics, most notably what appears to be a nearly constant blizzard1, breaking for an average of 1-2 hours daily. Analysis of this event has determined SCP-880 experiences no snowfall, and intense winds have produced various squalls which cause the illusion of a blizzard. Despite the potential of snow drifts within SCP-880, no level of snow deeper than sixteen (16) centimetres has been found within SCP-880 or in the surrounding area. Anything entering SCP-880 during a storm or within when a storm begins has so far proven to be irrevocably lost, despite extensive search and rescue efforts. GPS location fails shortly after a storm begins, transmission and rescue lines are cut, and radio communication becomes impossible due to overwhelming interference. Current tallies set the number of personnel lost to SCP-880 at 32.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

Footnotes
1. Due to the similarity of this phenomena to the abilites possessed by SCP-2082 investigation into a potential connection between the two objects is ongoing.

At first I thought "Oh boy, an isolated weather effect that kills those who stay too long." Probably had no effect on me because I've seen a desert variant in a Dungeons and Dragons book.

Then I read the second addendum.

And then I read the talk page and laughed, and wondered how I didn't see that before.

Impressive!

Analysis of observation of this event…

Could just say, "Observations of this event…"

Current tallies set the number of personnel lost to SCP-880 at 172.

These are people, not lemmings. A few go missing, the rest tend to catch on pretty quick. I don't see them continuing to send in personnel as opposed to ROVs after the first team is irrecoverably lost. I could understand maybe a tenth of that number, but approaching 200? That's just absurd.
